The disease is typically isolated, unilateral, and affects males, though a case linked a female carrier to a son with Norrie disease through a shared NDP missense mutation on chromosome Xp11.2. Analysis of enucleated eyes later found a somatic NDP mutation present only in retinal tissue, suggesting Coats telangiectasis results from localized norrin deficiency affecting retinal vasculogenesis.
